title: ML as strategic capability in investment industry
claim: ML has become critical competitive advantage in investment; digital data explosion drives adoption across idea generation, alpha design, asset allocation, position sizing, strategy evaluation
support: Field evolved from narrow trade execution automation to comprehensive algorithmic strategies
mechanism: ML enables processing of broader data sources than classical methods
validation: Compare ML-managed AUM vs discretionary

title: Tick data regularization prevents look-ahead bias
claim: Raw tick data must be regularized into uniform bars (time, volume, dollar) to avoid look-ahead bias from irregular event timing
support: ITCH order book data requires time-normalization to reflect real decision points
mechanism: Non-uniform tick intervals create phantom information leakage; regularization aligns features to decision frequency
validation: Walk-forward IC stability across bar sizes

title: Four-category factor framework for alpha engineering
claim: Alpha factors categorize into: (1) momentum/sentiment, (2) value, (3) volatility/size, (4) quality. Each has domain-specific metrics and economic rationale
support: Systematic framework linking factors to market inefficiencies and tradeable premia
mechanism: Each factor exploits distinct market behavior: momentum=underreaction, value=fundamental mispricing, volatility=leverage effects, quality=risk-adjusted returns
validation: Cross-validate across universes (US/intl, caps, sectors); test comovement

title: Three classes of backtest failure: data, implementation, overfitting
claim: Backtests fail via: (1) data biases (look-ahead, survivorship, outliers, unrepresentative periods), (2) implementation issues (mark-to-market timing, trading costs), (3) data-snooping and overfitting

source.section: How to avoid the pitfalls of backtesting

support: Taxonomy of failure modes linked to specific remedies (purging, embargoing, cost models, deflated SR)
mechanism: Look-ahead: using future data at decision time. Survivorship: excluding failed assets. Overfitting: parameter selection inflates expected OOS performance
validation: Walk-forward; in/out IC; Deflated SR analysis

title: Deflated Sharpe Ratio for backtest performance estimation
claim: Use deflated Sharpe Ratio to adjust reported SR for multiple hypothesis testing bias and estimate true out-of-sample performance likelihood
support: Bailey et al. framework addresses the multiple testing problem in quantitative research; provides statistical correction for backtest selection bias
mechanism: Deflated SR = in-sample SR * sqrt((1 - phi) / (N - 1)) where N=number of trials, phi=autocorrelation; lower values indicate higher overfitting risk
assumptions: SR estimation error follows predictable distribution
Trial count is known or estimated
failure_modes: Does not account for cross-strategy correlation
validation: Retrospective: compare deflated SR predictions to realized 2-3 year OOS returns

title: Time series cross-validation with purging and embargoing for trading models
claim: Standard K-fold CV causes look-ahead bias in time series; use purging (exclude training obs overlapping test), embargoing (exclude obs adjacent to test window), and combinatorial CV
support: de Prado framework explicitly addresses temporal leakage in ML backtests; implemented in MLearning library
mechanism: Standard CV leaks information through overlapping train/test periods; purging removes contamination, embargoing creates buffer for decision lag
assumptions: Sufficient data for buffering after purging
Test set is representative after filtering
validation: Walk-forward: measure IC/Sharpe drop when CV is vs isn't applied

title: Linear regression for returns forecasting: regularization and multicollinearity
claim: OLS linear regression for returns requires L1/L2 regularization (Lasso/Ridge) to handle multicollinearity in factors; unregularized OLS amplifies noise in correlated predictors
support: Regularized regression balances fit and generalization; Lasso feature selection, Ridge shrinkage
mechanism: Correlated features inflate coefficient standard errors and out-of-sample variance; L1 shrinkage to zero, L2 toward zero
assumptions: Linear relationship between factors and returns
Regularization hyperparameter tunable on validation set
validation: Walk-forward validation with expanding window

title: ARIMA/GARCH for volatility and autoregressive returns forecasting
claim: ARIMA models autoregressive returns patterns; GARCH models volatility clustering and mean-reversion; both require stationarity testing and lag-order selection
support: ARIMA captures short-term mean-reversion, GARCH captures volatility regimes and leverage effects
mechanism: Autocorrelated returns (AR) and errors (MA); variance depends on past shocks and variance (GARCH); useful for intraday/options strategies
assumptions: Series is stationary or can be differenced
Lag order can be identified via AIC/BIC
validation: Backtest volatility-adjusted position sizing using GARCH conditional vol

title: Bayesian methods for uncertainty quantification in trading models
claim: Bayesian inference provides posterior distributions over model parameters and predictions; useful for decision-making under uncertainty and adaptive strategy adjustment
support: Posterior distributions quantify belief updates from data; credible intervals replace frequentist confidence intervals for directional bets
mechanism: Prior belief + likelihood from data -> posterior; predictive distribution integrates over parameter uncertainty
validation: Backtest risk-adjusted positions using posterior credible intervals

title: Decision trees and random forests for factor importance and non-linear returns
claim: Decision trees capture non-linear relationships and interactions; random forests reduce overfitting via ensembling; feature importance from permutation/Gini measures factor relevance

source.section: Tree-based models: decision trees and ensembles

support: RF handles high-dimensional factor spaces and interactions automatically; importance scores guide factor selection
mechanism: Trees partition feature space; multiple uncorrelated trees average predictions and reduce variance; Gini split importance ranks factors
failure_modes: Importance may reflect collinearity not causation
validation: Backtest portfolio using top-K features by importance

title: Gradient Boosted Machines (GBM) for trading: sequential error correction and hyperparameter sensitivity
claim: GBM improves on weak learners via sequential error minimization; sensitive to learning rate, tree depth, and sample fraction; requires careful tuning and validation
support: GBM state-of-art for supervised learning; but prone to overfitting if hyperparameters not tuned properly
mechanism: Each tree fits residuals from prior trees; shrinkage and subsampling regularize; sequential updates can amplify overfitting in financial data
failure_modes: Learning rate too high->instability, too low->slow
validation: Walk-forward tuning; compare GBM to RF baseline

title: Unsupervised learning for portfolio construction: PCA, clustering, and cointegration
claim: PCA reduces dimensionality and identifies uncorrelated principal component portfolios; K-means clustering groups similar securities; cointegration identifies pairs for mean-reversion
support: Unsupervised methods uncover structure without labels; useful for risk factor discovery and asset grouping
mechanism: PCA: linear combinations of correlated factors. Clustering: segment assets by features. Cointegration: long-run equilibrium + mean-reversion trading
validation: Backtest cointegration pairs; measure P&L and Calmar ratio

title: Information Coefficient (IC) and Rank IC for factor alpha measurement
claim: IC = correlation(factor, next return); Rank IC = rank correlation; high IC (>0.05) indicates alpha, measured in-sample and out-of-sample for validation
support: IC is industry standard for factor evaluation; avoids backtest biases by measuring direct signal-return correlation
mechanism: IC measures predictive power independent of portfolio construction and costs; normalized by factor and return distributions
assumptions: IC is stable across time periods
IC translates to portfolio returns (depends on portfolio weight distribution)
failure_modes: IC estimates noisy with few observations
validation: Cross-validate IC across time windows; compare IC to backtest Sharpe

title: Market data quality: OHLCV aggregation, survivorship bias, and corporate actions
claim: Price data must account for splits, dividends, and delistings; survivorship bias (only successful companies in current data) biases backtest returns upward
support: Comprehensive data cleaning essential for valid backtests; poor-quality data inflates reported performance
mechanism: Splits adjust prices downward; dividends adjust prices and returns; delistings remove failed stocks from dataset; combined effect: reported returns are optimistic
validation: Verify adjustment factors against corporate action records

title: Alternative data evaluation: coverage, latency, cost, and predictive power
claim: Non-traditional data (satellite, credit card, web) may signal future returns; validate with IC measurement, cost analysis, and regime tests before integration
support: Alternative data offers informational edges but requires careful vetting; high cost may offset alpha
mechanism: Coverage: what % of universe, latency: delay vs real-time, cost: subscription + data processing, alpha: IC and Sharpe contribution
assumptions: IC from alt data is repeatable
Data is available over backtest window
failure_modes: Look-ahead bias in alt data timestamps
validation: Walk-forward: measure IC decay as more managers use data

title: Transaction costs, slippage, and impact in backtest modeling
claim: Realistic cost modeling (commissions, spreads, market impact) essential; omitting costs overestimates Sharpe by 0.5-2x; impact models scale with position size and liquidity
support: Most backtest failures trace to cost underestimation; live performance trails backtest sharply when costs neglected
mechanism: Commissions: fixed/percentage per trade. Spread: bid-ask cost. Impact: price moves proportional to position; scales nonlinearly with size
assumptions: Cost functions are linear or monotonic
Fills occur at midpoint or better
validation: Compare backtest-to-live PnL drop; audit cost assumptions

title: Bias-variance tradeoff and regularization in ML-based trading models
claim: Underfitting (high bias) misses alpha; overfitting (high variance) captures noise. Regularization, early stopping, and validation set selection balance tradeoff.
support: Fundamental ML principle; critical in finance where noise dominates in returns
mechanism: Bias from simplified model; variance from fitting to training noise. Regularization shrinks toward simpler model; validation prevents overfitting
validation: Compare in-sample to out-of-sample performance metrics

title: Multi-factor linear regression and collinearity diagnosis
claim: In multi-factor models, high VIF (variance inflation factor, >5) indicates collinearity; use correlation matrix and eigenvalue analysis to identify and remove redundant factors
support: Practical diagnostic for factor selection; prevents unstable coefficient estimates and poor OOS generalization
mechanism: VIF = 1 / (1 - R^2) for each factor regressed on others; high VIF means factor is linear combination of others
assumptions: Removing correlated factors doesn't lose alpha
validation: Walk-forward: track correlation matrix stability and factor weights

title: NLP and sentiment analysis for trading: text preprocessing, feature extraction, and model selection
claim: Extract sentiment from news, social media, earnings calls; preprocess (tokenization, stopwords, stemming), vectorize (TF-IDF, embeddings), and model with SVM, Naive Bayes, or RNNs
support: Text sentiment correlates with short-term price movements; integration with quantitative signals improves Sharpe
mechanism: Sentiment scores from text models fed to portfolio allocation or rank-weighting; lagged sentiment captures market psychology
assumptions: Sentiment is predictive of next return
Model generalizes across periods and topics
failure_modes: Model overfitting to historical sentiment-return correlation
validation: Walk-forward validation; check for crowding effect (IC decay)

title: Topic modeling and latent semantic analysis for thematic portfolio construction
claim: Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and Non-negative Matrix Factorization (NMF) extract topics from documents; topics can signal sector trends and correlated risk factors
support: Unsupervised discovery of document structure; enables thematic portfolio tilting and risk factor identification
mechanism: LDA: generative model with document-topic and topic-word distributions. NMF: factorization into non-negative components
assumptions: Optimal number of topics is identifiable
validation: Cross-validate topic stability; check out-of-sample coherence

title: Word embeddings and semantic similarity for feature engineering
claim: Word2Vec, GloVe, and contextual embeddings (BERT) encode semantic meaning; embeddings capture industry relationships, thematic coherence, and text-based alpha signals

source.section: Word embeddings and neural networks for NLP

support: Embeddings preserve linguistic relationships; enable vector-based portfolio similarity, sector clustering, and similarity-based trading signals
mechanism: Embeddings trained on large text corpora; semantic similarity via cosine distance; enables transfer learning to new text domains
assumptions: Semantic relationships correlate with tradeable patterns
failure_modes: Domain shift (embeddings trained on general text, applied to finance)
Crowding effect from widespread embedding use
validation: Out-of-sample test: compare embedding-based signals to baseline

title: Hyperparameter tuning: grid search, randomized search, and Bayesian optimization
claim: Systematic hyperparameter search essential; grid search exhaustive but slow, random search efficient, Bayesian optimization balances exploration/exploitation
support: Hyperparameter selection strongly affects model performance; careless tuning leads to severe overfitting
mechanism: Grid: evaluate all combinations in grid. Random: sample uniformly. Bayesian: model performance surface, sample high-promise regions
assumptions: Tuning effort is justified by performance gain
validation: Cross-validate hyperparameters; measure sensitivity to tuning set

title: Alphalens factor tearsheet for systematic factor evaluation
claim: Use Alphalens to compute IC, Sharpe, returns attribution by quantile and day-lag; identify factor decay and crowding effects
support: Alphalens open-source; enables reproducible factor validation without backtest artifacts
mechanism: Ranks factors, computes returns in forward windows, aggregates by quantile and lag, produces comprehensive diagnostics
validation: Cross-validate IC across time splits

title: Hierarchical clustering and dendrogram-based portfolio construction
claim: Hierarchical clustering groups correlated assets; dendrogram linkage methods (single, complete, average) affect grouping; enables minimum-variance portfolio at cluster level
support: Hierarchical clustering provides interpretable asset grouping; can improve risk-adjusted returns
mechanism: Agglomerative clustering: merge most similar pairs recursively; dendrogram visualizes hierarchy; cut at desired granularity
validation: Walk-forward clustering; measure realized correlation structure

title: Feature importance from tree ensembles: Gini vs. permutation importance
claim: Gini importance (split reduction) biased toward high-cardinality features; permutation importance (OOB prediction drop) is model-agnostic and more reliable for trading factors
support: Permutation importance avoids Gini bias; enables fair comparison across factor types (continuous, categorical)
mechanism: Gini: split information gain in tree. Permutation: shuffle feature, measure OOB error increase
failure_modes: OOB error not reliable with small datasets
validation: Measure IC of top factors by each importance metric

title: Walk-forward analysis and forward-looking bias in backtest optimization
claim: Standard backtest with parameter optimization on full history is forward-looking; walk-forward (expanding train, test on next period) prevents look-ahead bias in hyperparameter selection
support: Walk-forward is only defensible method for parameter optimization; otherwise backtest is invalid
mechanism: Expanding train window 1..T, validate T+1..T+K; retune parameters on each window
assumptions: Parameters optimized on future data are invalid
validation: Audit backtest code: confirm walk-forward structure

title: Stationarity testing and differencing for time series models
claim: Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) test identifies unit root (non-stationarity); differencing (first/seasonal) removes trend; stationarity required for ARIMA and many models

source.section: Time series preprocessing: stationarity and differencing

support: Stationarity assumption critical for model validity; violation leads to spurious regression
mechanism: ADF tests H0: unit root present. P-value < 0.05: reject null, series is stationary. Differencing: X(t) = Y(t) - Y(t-1)
assumptions: Differenced series is suitable for modeling
failure_modes: ADF p-value unreliable with short series
validation: Train ARIMA on differenced series; check residuals for remaining autocorrelation

title: XGBoost and LightGBM: efficient gradient boosting for large-scale factor modeling
claim: XGBoost and LightGBM are production-grade GBM implementations with GPU support and built-in regularization; outperform hand-coded GBM on speed and generalization
support: Industrial standard; implemented in major trading platforms and research workflows
mechanism: XGBoost: L-BFGS optimizer, column subsampling. LightGBM: leaf-wise growth, GPU acceleration
assumptions: Data fits in memory or distributed storage
validation: Compare OOS Sharpe and training time

title: Factor crowding and mean reversion of alpha as strategy popularity increases
claim: Factors exhibit alpha decay over time; crowding (many managers implement same factor) compresses returns and increases correlation; diversification across factors mitigates
support: Empirical finding: published factor premiums decay after research visibility; alpha is finite and consumable
mechanism: Crowding: increased AUM chasing same signal, increased slippage and market impact, reduced alpha per unit capital
failure_modes: Crowding effect varies by factor type
validation: Backtest: simulate increasing AUM impact

title: Bid-ask spread, volume, and liquidity regime effects on trading signals
claim: Liquid assets (low spread, high volume) enable low-cost execution; illiquid regimes increase slippage; signal IC varies by liquidity; liquid subset may outperform due to lower costs
support: Liquidity is primary execution constraint; trading cost model essential for live performance
mechanism: Spread cost: (ask - bid) / mid. Slippage: (execution - mid) / mid. Both scale nonlinearly with order size
assumptions: Cost is proportional to liquidity metric
validation: Compare backtest to live execution cost

title: Copula models and tail dependence for portfolio construction
claim: Copulas model joint distributions of asset returns; tail dependence captures co-crash risk; useful for extreme risk management and drawdown minimization
support: Captures non-linear dependence missed by correlation; critical for tail risk
mechanism: Copula: joint distribution independent of marginals; enables separate modeling of extremes and normal regime
validation: Backtest during market crises; measure maximum drawdown

title: Machine learning pipeline for quantitative trading: data -> features -> model -> backtest -> deployment
claim: Structured workflow prevents data leakage and ensures reproducibility; each stage must validate before proceeding to next
support: Systematic pipeline design reduces operational risk and enables scaling
mechanism: Data cleaning -> feature engineering (alignment, lag) -> model selection/tuning (CV) -> backtest (walk-forward) -> live deployment
validation: Compare backtest-to-live performance; verify pipeline determinism

title: Lookahead bias and temporal alignment in factor and alternative data integration
claim: Factor release dates must precede decision times; alternative data timestamps subject to backfill; use trade date + N day lag, not price date, for alignment
support: Temporal misalignment is subtle and pervasive source of backtest overfitting; critical for credibility
mechanism: Earnings announced after market close (day T); backtest must use day T+1 close or day T+2 open, not day T close
failure_modes: Backfill in alt data (values updated retroactively)
validation: Rerun backtest with enforced lag; measure performance delta

title: Logistic regression for classification and position sizing in directional strategies
claim: Logistic regression outputs probability of up/down move; useful for position sizing and stop-loss automation; calibration essential (predicted prob matches realized freq)
support: Probabilistic output enables confidence-weighted position sizing; more nuanced than binary signals
mechanism: Sigmoid: P(y=1) = 1/(1+exp(-z)); output in [0,1]; calibration: predicted prob = realized freq
failure_modes: Probability estimates unstable in new regimes
validation: Backtest with position sizing by predicted probability

title: Combinatorial purged K-fold for unbiased ML model selection in backtests
claim: Combinatorial purged cross-validation (CPV) extends time-series CV with multiple train/test combinatorial splits; reduces variance of CV estimate
support: CPV provides more stable CV scores than single split; reduces overconfidence in model selection
mechanism: Multiple combinatorial purged splits; aggregate CV scores across splits; reduces noise
assumptions: Data is sufficient for many splits
validation: Cross-validate stability across different CPV configurations

title: Sentiment model drift and domain shift in deployed NLP systems
claim: Sentiment models trained on historical text may not generalize to new topics, events, or linguistic style changes; monitor model performance and retrain when drift detected
support: Model drift is primary source of live performance degradation in NLP-based strategies
mechanism: Language evolves (new slang), topics shift (pandemic, war), style changes (formal vs. casual); model trained on past text misclassifies new text
validation: Backtest sentiment model trained on 1-3 year windows; compare accuracy

title: Cross-validation strategy selection and nested CV for honest performance estimation
claim: Inner CV tunes hyperparameters; outer CV estimates generalization error; nested CV is only unbiased method
support: Nested CV prevents data snooping in hyperparameter selection; expensive but necessary for credible estimates
mechanism: Outer loop: split into train/test. Inner loop (on train): tune hyperparameters via CV. Report outer loop test error
failure_modes: Overfitting still possible if inner CV underfits
validation: Backtest both; compare OOS Sharpe to nested CV estimate

title: Stacking and blending for ensemble returns prediction
claim: Stacking: train meta-learner on base model predictions; blending: holdout set to train meta-learner; both combine weak learners into stronger ensemble
support: Ensembling multiple models often outperforms single best model; meta-learner learns to weight predictions
mechanism: Base models: RF, GBM, linear reg. Meta-learner: logistic reg or ridge on base outputs. Avoids overfitting via validation holdout
failure_modes: Base model correlation reduces ensemble benefit
validation: Compare ensemble IC to individual base model IC

title: Dimensionality reduction via PCA and variance preservation trade-off
claim: PCA retains k principal components explaining desired variance (e.g., 95%); reduces collinearity and computational cost; but loses interpretability
support: PCA is standard unsupervised dimensionality reduction; balances noise reduction and information retention
mechanism: Eigenvector decomposition of covariance; ordered by eigenvalue (explained variance); select cumulative variance threshold
validation: Plot cumulative explained variance; select k at elbow

title: Zipline backtesting framework: event-driven simulation and reproducibility
claim: Zipline is open-source backtester with event-driven architecture; enables reproducible, modular strategy development; integrated with Alphalens for factor analysis
support: Zipline is de facto standard for open-source Python backtesting; widely adopted in academic and industry research
mechanism: Event-driven: loop through market events (OHLC bars); execute trading logic; track positions and P&L
failure_modes: Zipline version changes break existing code
validation: Compare Zipline backtest to manual calculation
